title: Claude Camus de Pontcarré to Villeroy, March-June 1586: cipher passages in BnF fr. 15572 ff. 111v-272v (Camus's cipher)

steps.what: Michael Brackx (issue #91): Tomokiyo's henryiii page ('Camus's Cipher') lists the leaves and gives the key table and one opening phrase that matches none of the blocks; no modern reading found in this repository or on the web.
Gallica full-size IIIF images of BnF fr. 15572 (ark btv1b9061879d), canvases 118, 140, 142, 158, 281-282.
Tomokiyo's table encoded as labels with values, codes and nulls.
Every block transcribed sign by sign from full-size line strips with the x-position of each sign (Brackx with Claude Opus 5.5); margin decipherments and interlinear glosses re-read at full zoom.

Beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram, scored by crib agreement (gapped alignment) against the margin decipherments and by corpus-word coverage, each against shuffled-key controls; passes until nothing changed: one shared label set, a line-by-line proofread (missing lines 134v A l. 5, B l. 1 found), contact sheets to split look-alikes, values adopted only with two or more contexts.
Blind re-transcription of the cribbed blocks: 76-95% token agreement with the first transcription; 22 changes accepted after checking the image.
Corpus-word coverage of the decode posted as 79.3% over all blocks (three shuffled keys 37.1-47.1%).

Brackx's correction to the language model: it had been built from Gutenberg 48529-48531, of which only 48529 is Montaigne (48530 is Italian, 48531 a Middle English romance); rebuilt from the Essais I-III (48529, 49168, 58801), coverage over all blocks falls from 79.3% to 74.6%, against 36-50% for five shuffled keys. The crib agreements do not use the model and are unchanged.

Readings of the five cribbed blocks in the writer's spelling with English (issue #91 comment): each word carried by the figures or the contemporary decipherment, figures followed where they differ (Comont, s'effectuera, lundy et sans); label legend with sign shapes.

Measured with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure (in-word bracket expansions count as holes): f. 111v 0.961, f. 112r 0.974, f. 151r middle block 0.963 (read); f. 134v B 0.781, C 0.812 (read in part). ff. 132v, 134v A, the f. 151r margin and foot blocks and ff. 272r-v give phrases between gaps: decoded, not read. Reviewed as sentences (grade B) by Claude Opus 5.5.

Brackx checked serment on f. 112r on the image (issue #95): -ment ne rests on the figures (a = m, θ = t, q = e) and the interlinear glosses ent and ne; the first three signs ʃ ρ r have no gloss and the key gives m, i/s, a/e, so ser- rests on the margin alone. Reading changed from [?serment] to [?ser]ment; read_share unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: The blocks that read rest on the contemporary margin and interlinear decipherments; Tomokiyo's key, corrected and extended by Michael Brackx, was applied to the figures as a check and decides where figures and margin differ.

gaps.item: f. 111v: the three groups after 'car ie uous' at the end of the block
gaps.detail: they run past the margin decipherment; no second context

gaps.item: f. 134v B: the name after 'sauue' (margin C?main, cipher 7 z fa qn es) and the doubtful sur, Frenac, peult, on
gaps.detail: the margin paraphrases the opening and does not match the figures

gaps.item: f. 134v C: the last group and the doubtful et, le
gaps.detail: single signs (?sb2, ?14) at the end of the block, one context each

gaps.item: ff. 132v, 134v A, 151r margin and foot blocks, 272r-v: decoded, not read
gaps.detail: no contemporary decipherment (134v A and the 151r margin only paraphrased); the plain 9 and y still carry three values each and contact sheets show no further split at this resolution

gaps.item: 57 unvalued labels (108 tokens), probably nomenclator codes, among them the group for 'cy faict' on 134v A
gaps.detail: mostly single tokens with no crib context; Tomokiyo's table has no values for them

outcome.notes: Contributed by Michael Brackx (issue #91, 22-23 Oct 2026). Three blocks reach the read bar on the contemporary decipherment; the language-model coverage figure is corrected from 79.3% to 74.6% (Essais I-III model).

texts.label: f. 111v
texts.summary: Camus to Villeroy from Castets, 21 March 1586: the old carrier to 'le parent', the secret contact, can no longer help; Camus asks for orders for the service of 'the lord you know of'.

reading_review.note: Coherent sentences following the margin decipherment; the three groups after 'car ie uous' run past the margin text.

texts.label: f. 112r
texts.summary: The same letter continued: Villeroy should send separate packets ciphered with the memorandum Camus left, with code names 'le beau frere' or 'le porteur' for the carrier and 'le seruiteur' or 'l'oblige' for Camus.

reading_review.note: Coherent sentences following the margin decipherment; [?serment] and [?et] doubtful.

texts.label: f. 132v
texts.summary: Castets, 1 April 1586: phrases about the bearer and the 'poursuivant'; no contemporary decipherment.

texts.label: f. 134v, block A
texts.summary: Bordeaux, early April 1586: seeing the bearer, something to be presented to the 'poursuivant'; the margin paraphrases.

texts.label: f. 134v, block B
texts.summary: Talk of the 'demande de Frenac' and of the treaty at Caumont, which cannot be saved.

reading_review.note: The margin paraphrases the opening; the name after 'sauue' unread; 7 holes in 32 words.

texts.label: f. 134v, block C
texts.summary: The bearer gives very little hope of relief (secours) from his journey.

reading_review.note: The margin note carries the sentence; the end of the block unread.

texts.label: f. 151r, middle block
texts.summary: Bordeaux, 12 April 1586: seeing the bearer is Camus's excuse to arrange 'la partie que scauez', which he hopes will be carried out on Monday without suspicion.

reading_review.note: One coherent sentence; the figures give 'subson' where the margin has 'soupcon'.

texts.label: f. 151r, margin and foot blocks
texts.summary: Courtesies and a note about 'l'amy'; the margin block has a free clear version, the foot block's crib has an unread first line.

texts.label: ff. 272r-v
texts.summary: La Rochelle, June 1586: men sent to see Camus about their part with 'le parent', without telling him anything particular; Camus asks to be relieved and withdrawn.

prior.where: Contemporary decipherments on the leaves: interlinear glosses and full margin texts for ff. 111v-112r, margin notes for f. 134v A-C and f. 151r. Tomokiyo (Cryptiana, henryiii) gives the key table and the leaf list, no reading of the blocks. No modern reading found (Brackx, issue #91).

human: Contributed: Michael Brackx (issue #91, 22-23 Oct 2026) transcribed, decoded and read the blocks with Claude Code outside the project; the project asked for the full texts under the read bar, measured and reviewed them, and wrote them up.
